name: The Bekaa valley, 24 July 1982: F-4Es come over the mountains
description: The first combat use of the Osa over the Bekaa (roadmap 10.2): the vehicle stands deployed on the valley floor, mountains on both sides. A pair of F-4E Phantoms comes from the west over the Lebanon range, hidden behind the ridge until it tops it, and dives into the valley to attack the sites just north of the vehicle. On 24 July 1982 a Syrian Osa shot down an F-4E over the Bekaa; here the crew has the minute between the pair coming over the crest and its attack. The NPC commander runs the crew; take any seat, or his.
notes: The event: wapo_1982 (a Syrian SA-8 shoots down an Israeli F-4 on 24 July 1982; the missile sites are then attacked), docs/research/OSA_RESEARCH_2026-10.md section 9. Everything else is SAM3D's: the vehicle's place, the valley drawn as two straight ridges (the Lebanon range west, the Anti-Lebanon east; their heights and widths are PLACEHOLDERS), the F-4Es' route, heights, speed and echo, and their warning receiver (NATO's class receiver from em/nato_1985.json stands in for whatever they carried). Cesium's ground replaces the ridges when the scenario is played on the map.

ridges.notes: The Lebanon range: crest 16 km west, 1500 m above the valley floor. Placeholder.
The Anti-Lebanon: crest 15 km east, 1200 m above the floor. Placeholder.

targets.notes: Over the crest 400 m above it, down into the valley, the attack on the sites 3.5 km north of the vehicle, out to the north-east and back west. Placeholder.
